title: Two points on the equator, 90° apart
caption: Seen from above the pole, the equator is a circle of radius R = 6,371 km. Points at longitudes 0° and 90° make a central angle of 90° = π/2, so the great-circle distance is R × π/2 ≈ 10,008 km.
alt: The equator as a circle with two points on it, at longitude 0° and longitude 90°, joined to the centre with a right angle between the radii.
description: Look down on the equator: a circle of radius R = 6,371 km.
The points at 0° and 90° longitude are a quarter of the way round.
The central angle is 90° = π/2 radians, so the arc length is 6,371 × π/2 ≈ 10,008 km.
